$comment: Reviewer registry for dotf pr triage-queue (#28): did a review actually happen on a PR?
Adapted from mlorentedev/dotfiles harness/review-attestation.json, where each rule is reasoned.
Registry only: no workflow here turns it into a required status (owner decision 2026-11-05).

reviewers.why: ADVISORY (2026-08-22): its review still attests, but its DECLINE no longer refuses.
review_markers: No actionable comments were generated in the recent review

reviewers.why: PR-Agent (TOOL-013, #786/#1032) posts as github-actions via GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the comments API, not the reviews API — so reviews[] is empty on a PR it genuinely reviewed.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding silently is not.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: The release PR restates commits already on main, each reviewed when it merged. Release PRs #20 and #23 changed exactly these two paths.

triage.standing_why: Who may write the triage record, so a marker from any commenter cannot clear the queue.
triage.why: A disposition recorded on the PR is durable and machine-readable; one in a chat message is not.

classification.why: A finding's class is read from a whole line equal to prefix + class, never parsed out of prose; a finding with no such line, or two that disagree, is unclassified and goes to a human. .pr_agent.toml asks the reviewer for exactly these lines, and tests/harness.bats fails if the two drift apart. reviewers names PR-Agent (github-actions) only, because CodeRabbit writes its own severity format. Shape copied from dotfiles (TOOL-017).
